title: Finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons with process tensors
abstract: We develop a process tensor approach for calculating the finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons. We show that the finite-temperature phonon influence functional can be expressed as the elementwise exponential of a low-rank matrix product state, enabling an efficient summation of electron worldlines. An embedding construction embeds worldlines of different propagation times into a single matrix product state. This construction yields the propagator over the full simulated time interval in a single calculation. We benchmark this approach against available finite-temperature density-matrix renormalization group results for the one-dimensional Holstein polaron. We further obtain numerically converged spectra for the two-dimensional Holstein polaron. The spectra reveal a progressive transfer of spectral weight from coherent spectral features into an incoherent background with increasing temperature.
summary: This work introduces a novel process tensor approach to calculate the finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons. By mapping the phonon influence functional onto a low-rank Matrix Product State, the authors achieve an efficient and numerically exact calculation. The results confirm the temperature-driven decoherence of quasiparticle features in these strongly correlated electron-phonon systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex theoretical challenge of calculating the finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons, which are quasiparticles formed by electron-phonon coupling.
main_result: The authors successfully developed a process tensor approach that yields numerically converged spectra for both 1D and 2D Holstein polarons, showing a clear transfer of spectral weight to an incoherent background with increasing temperature.
method: The core method involves representing the finite-temperature phonon influence functional as the elementwise exponential of a low-rank Matrix Product State (MPS), enabling efficient summation of electron worldlines.
model_or_system: The system studied is the lattice polaron, modeled using the Holstein Hamiltonian, which describes a charge carrier coupled to lattice vibrations (phonons). This is relevant for materials like perovskites and organic semiconductors.
key_observables: The primary observable is the single-particle spectral function, accessible via Angle-Resolved Photoemission (ARPES), and the retarded single-electron Green's function.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the electron-phonon coupling constant (lambda), the temperature (T or beta), and the dimensionality (1D and 2D).
main_assumptions: The method relies on expressing the phonon influence functional as a low-rank MPS and uses an embedding construction to efficiently calculate the full time evolution.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the flow-equation approach, showing the propagator approximated by an MPS. Figure 8 demonstrates the spectral functions of the 1D Holstein polaron across a wide temperature range.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon zero-temperature path integral methods, extends them to finite temperature via thermal averaging, and introduces a process tensor approach using MPS to solve the resulting flow equation, benchmarking results against DMRG.
why_interesting: The use of advanced tensor network techniques (MPS/MPO) to tackle finite-temperature, non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated electron-phonon systems is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and material properties.
